intro: Above the components sits Kimen's GenUI layer: agents emit JSON UI specs
(data, never code), the neutral catalog validates them against the
published component surface, and the guarded renderer turns accepted
specs into DOM. Protocol adapters translate external vocabularies into
that neutral core and are disposable by design; the catalog and the
ki-* elements are the durable assets. These packages live in this

packages.whenToUse: Any boundary where agent-emitted JSON must become Kimen UI: validate specs standalone, render them with the guardrail enforced, or stream them progressively. Both protocol adapters and any custom transport build on it.
packages.whenNotToUse: Hand-authored pages that never render agent output — use @kimen/elements directly.

entryPoints.name: validateUiSpec
entryPoints.summary: Accepts or rejects an agent-emitted UI spec against the catalog in use — the built-in generated catalog, or a registered one passed as options.catalog — before anything renders. The report lists every issue with a code (unknown-component, unknown-prop, invalid-prop-type, unknown-slot, undeclared-action, forbidden-key, size-budget, depth-budget, malformed-spec), a path into the spec document and the offending value.

entryPoints.name: renderUiSpec
entryPoints.summary: Validates and renders a spec into options.surface through the guarded renderer: only components of the catalog in use render (options.catalog selects it; absent, the built-in catalog applies), only actions declared in the spec dispatch (delivered as data to options.onAction), unknown props are rejected and no code path executes from spec data. Failures come back as diagnostics naming rule, path and value; nothing attaches on failure.

entryPoints.name: createStreamingRenderer
entryPoints.summary: Progressive rendering over a streamed spec: each push(node) validates one top-level subtree and attaches it only when fully valid; an invalid node fails closed while previously attached content remains, and the render budgets bind the accumulated stream. The catalog in use is fixed at creation via options.catalog.

entryPoints.name: createCatalog
entryPoints.summary: Registers your own components behind a data-only JSON facade — the exact entry shape of the generated catalog (tag, usage guidance, typed prop constraints, slots, events) — and returns a deeply frozen catalog that validateUiSpec and both renderers accept via options.catalog. The definition is untrusted input: it crosses the same purity wall as UI specs, tags must be conservative custom-element names, collisions with the extended catalog fail closed, usage guidance is mandatory, and every rejection is a RegistrationIssue naming code, path and offender. Pass { extend: catalogData } to compose with the built-in components, or omit it for a standalone catalog.

entryPoints.name: DEFAULT_RENDER_BUDGETS
entryPoints.summary: The declared render budgets (maxDepth 32, maxNodes 512, maxBytes 262144). A spec exactly at a budget passes; one beyond it is rejected before any node attaches. Hosts may tighten them via options.budgets; the renderer never renders past them. Standalone validation has its own ceilings, VALIDATION_MAX_BYTES (262144 UTF-8 bytes, overridable per call with maxBytes) and VALIDATION_MAX_DEPTH (256).

entryPoints.name: catalogData
entryPoints.summary: The generated catalog document itself: one entry per published ki-* element with typed props, events, slots and when-to-use guidance, plus the elements version it derives from. Its schema version is exported as CATALOG_SCHEMA_VERSION.

packages.whenToUse: Configure ANY LLM to emit valid Kimen UI specs: derive a system prompt, a catalog-specialized JSON Schema (with provider-strict lowerings) or a tool definition from the catalog in use — built-in or registered — and close the reliability loop with normalization and a single-round repair message.
packages.whenNotToUse: Enforcement: the artifacts are advisory. Validation and rendering stay in @kimen/catalog; hosts that already emit valid specs need nothing from this package.

entryPoints.name: catalogPrompt
entryPoints.summary: Model-facing prompt: format rules, every component's when-to-use and when-NOT-to-use guidance verbatim, props with enums inline, and one example spec that validates against the same catalog. The universal fallback — works with any model, no structured-output support required.

entryPoints.name: uiSpecJsonSchema
entryPoints.summary: The neutral UI-spec format specialized to the catalog as a JSON Schema document: one branch per component, closed props and enums, closed objects everywhere. Targets: draft-2020-12 (default), openai-strict (all-required closed objects, recursion via $ref, documented provider limits enforced with named offenders), anthropic-strict (recursion-free, node tree unrolled to a bounded depth). Deterministic and version-stamped; fail-closed on skew, bad subsets and exceeded limits — never a silent truncation.

entryPoints.name: uiSpecTool
entryPoints.summary: Provider-neutral tool definition { name: 'emit_ui', description, inputSchema } wrapping exactly the lowered schema for the same options; maps mechanically onto any provider's tool or function surface.

entryPoints.name: normalizeEmission
entryPoints.summary: Strips the placeholders strict-mode all-required schemas force a model to emit (null-valued props, null action bindings, empty props containers) and touches nothing else. Pure cleanup over a fresh clone; output is untrusted until validateUiSpec passes.

entryPoints.name: repairPrompt
entryPoints.summary: Formats a failed ValidationReport into ONE corrective message naming every issue's code, path and offender, or null when the report is ok. The single-round-then-fail-closed policy is fixed.

packages.whenToUse: Your agent runtime speaks the A2UI protocol and its surfaces should render as Kimen components with the guardrail enforced.
packages.whenNotToUse: The agent can emit neutral Kimen UI specs directly (use @kimen/catalog alone), or the host is an MCP Apps client (use @kimen/adapter-mcp-apps).

entryPoints.name: createA2uiAdapter
entryPoints.summary: Creates the translation boundary: adapter.apply(message) turns declarative A2UI messages (surfaceUpdate, dataModelUpdate, beginRendering, deleteSurface) into neutral UI specs rendered only through the guarded renderer. User interactions return through options.onUserAction as A2UI userAction payloads; unmapped protocol constructs degrade to data reported through options.onDegradation.

entryPoints.name: SUPPORTED_A2UI_VERSIONS
entryPoints.summary: The exact A2UI protocol versions this adapter supports, versioned with the adapter in COMPAT.md.

entryPoints.name: A2UI_COVERAGE
entryPoints.summary: Machine-readable coverage table declaring how each A2UI component type is handled: mapped to a catalog component, rendered inline, or forbidden.

packages.whenToUse: You ship an MCP server and want tool results to render as interactive Kimen surfaces in MCP Apps (SEP-1865) hosts.
packages.whenNotToUse: The host is not an MCP Apps client, or you control the rendering surface directly — render neutral specs with @kimen/catalog instead.

entryPoints.name: declareToolSurface
entryPoints.summary: Declares in an MCP tool's _meta that its results render in a predeclared ui:// surface.

entryPoints.name: createKimenSurfaceResource
entryPoints.summary: The self-contained ui:// resource the server serves: one HTML document with every script and style inline, a no-network content policy, and the guarded renderer as its only render path.

entryPoints.name: surfaceToolResult
entryPoints.summary: Wraps a neutral UI spec plus a plain-text fallback as an MCP tool result, so hosts without interactive surfaces still get text.

entryPoints.name: createSurfaceBridge
entryPoints.summary: Runs inside the surface document: validates inbound JSON-RPC envelopes, renders ui/toolResult specs through the guarded renderer and dispatches only the surface's declared actions back to the host; non-protocol messages are ignored with no state change.

entryPoints.name: MCP_APPS_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS
entryPoints.summary: The exact MCP Apps protocol revisions this adapter supports, versioned with the adapter in COMPAT.md.
